answer: Each agent can earn a nontransferable reputation only by completing jobs whose outputs are checked by randomly selected peers, with a small stake held in a vault until disputes are resolved. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one identity into many does not multiply trusted work; each must separately earn endorsements and risk stake. On the tundra of a fresh network, attackers can still create hollow accounts, but making them credible requires funding and passing the same costly checks repeatedly.
